result.title: GRAFT: Execution-Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design
result.summary: Automated agent design searches for executable architectures that improve LLM-based agent performance, with evolutionary methods using language-model crossover to recombine promising mechanisms for task decomposition, model coordination, and verification. This search, however, is typically guided by aggregate fitness alone, which hides the instance-level successes and failures behind each score. We introduce Execution Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design (GRAFT), which uses aggregate fitness for selection and survival and parent-specific execution evidence to guide semantic crossover with integrated mutation. Its feedback harness reuses bounded samples of successful and failed runs from fitness evaluation, withholding reference answers and requiring no additional task executions. We evaluate GRAFT across six reasoning and programming settings using open-weight optimizer and executor models. It achieves a mean test accuracy of 82.0%, exceeding the strongest baseline by 9.8% points. Controlled ablations show that adding execution evidence improves test accuracy with initialization, search rules, repair policies, and evaluation budgets held fixed. Our results support the value of parent-specific execution evidence for evolutionary agent design.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GRAFT，用进化方法自动搜索可执行的 LLM agent 架构：以聚合适应度做选择与存活，同时复用评估中出现过的成败样例作为父代专属执行证据，引导语义交叉与变异。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用实例级成功／失败执行证据替代单一聚合得分来指导结构重组，可能为 latent 推理的贡献分配与验证信号设计提供线索，但论文面向纯文本 agent 架构搜索、无视觉状态，可供核查迁移空间。
